subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram partial-stream finalization lacks clear delivery-mode observability (sent vs preview-finalized vs canceled)

question: Should this Telegram issue be resolved by landing the focused partial-stream fix, by folding the behavior into the broader durable final-delivery contract, or by limiting the change to observability and hook parity?
rationale: The source-backed bug is real, but the permanent boundary affects Telegram delivery completion, operator observability, hook semantics, and broader cross-channel final-delivery contracts, so automation should not choose the product/API shape while overlapping PRs remain open.

options.title: Land A Focused Telegram Fix
options.body: Rebase or replace the linked Telegram PR, require redacted real Telegram proof, and keep broader cross-channel semantics tracked separately.

options.title: Fold Into Durable Delivery Contract
options.body: Pause this issue behind https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87561 so Telegram follows one shared final-delivery outcome contract with other channels.

options.title: Observability-Only Slice
options.body: Add explicit logs/events for Telegram preview-finalized, retained, canceled, failed, and skipped outcomes while deferring delivery-confirmation semantics.

recommendation.title: Land A Focused Telegram Fix
recommendation.body: Rebase or replace the linked Telegram PR, require redacted real Telegram proof, and keep broader cross-channel semantics tracked separately.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main ownership signals cover Telegram dispatch, streaming config, delivery tests, and release-adjacent work in the affected files.
